function: Federated learning over the air: aggregation of masked momentum and gradient updates by OTA computation, with MMSE aggregation receiver and transmit beamformer and a masking-aware MMSE bound (pp. 5-8).
system: Multi-antenna OTA uplink: 64 transmit antennas per client, 64 receive antennas at BS server, 10 clients, path-loss exponent 1.8; no RIS; band not stated (Table II, p. 10).
method: Federated learning (FedAvg-based, regularized least-squares regression model) with local and global momentum, thresholded masking of uploads, fair-weighted aggregation, semi-asynchronous client selection; supervised, federated (pp. 5-8, 10).
data_channel: MNIST (60,000 train, 10,000 test) for the learning task; channel simulated as massive-MIMO with path-loss exponent 1.8, no named standard model or dataset (pp. 8, 10).
test_conditions: One FL run per setting: i.i.d. or non-i.i.d. data, high/moderate/low computational diversity, mask thresholds; 10 clients (10 to 50 in Fig. 3); standard MNIST test set (pp. 10-12).
baselines: FullySyn, SemiSyn, FullyAsyn uploading policies; baselines of [30] (no momentum, no mask) and [39] (momentum, no mask), i.e. the framework with modules off; FWA versus w/oFWA (pp. 11-12).
metrics: Prediction accuracy versus running time, aggregation MMSE, communication number per round, training loss (Figs. 3-8, pp. 10-12).
complexity: Communication cost orders only: O(d) per client per round, O(S_k d) for SemiAsyn, total cost to a target accuracy; no cost of aggregation, transceiver or beamformer (pp. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 8: "denotes the path loss"; the only channel description is a path-loss exponent (kappa = 1.8, Table II, p. 10) with asymptotically orthogonal massive-MIMO channels; no standardized or measured channel is named.
q2_support: p. 10: "training dataset is 60000, and the size of the test dataset is 10000"; each setting (i.i.d. or non-i.i.d. data, computational diversity, mask threshold) is a separate FL run tested on the standard MNIST test split, with no unseen scenario or adaptation reported.
q3_support: p. 11: "refers to the baseline in [30] that does not incorporate momentum"; the baselines of [30] and [39] are the proposed framework with momentum and/or masking switched off, the other comparisons are uploading policies and FWA versus w/oFWA, and no non-learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 9: "Each communication round incurs O(d)"; the orders count uploaded model parameters (communication volume, model size d), and no operation count, runtime or complexity of the aggregation, transceiver or beamformer is reported.
q5_support: p. 10: "we use the MNIST"; MNIST is a public dataset of the learning task alone, the channel is simulated, and the paper gives no code or data link.
notes: Included as area 7, borderline: most contributions are on the FL side (momentum, mask, fair-weighted aggregation, client selection), but the mask is analyzed through the OTA aggregation MMSE (Proposition 2, p. 8) with an MMSE receiver and transmit beamformer (p. 8), so it is not excluded as above-PHY. q4 = 0 because the O(d) orders (p. 9) are model-size and upload volume; the running-time axis of Figs. 3, 7, 8 follows simulated client times t_i (Eq. 3, p. 5). Reviewer may confirm q3 and q4.
